questions.explain: Density ρ = m/V: mass divided by volume. Its standard unit is kg/m³.

questions.q: A force of 200 N acts on an area of 0.50 m². Calculate the pressure.
questions.explain: p = F/A = 200 ÷ 0.50 = 400 Pa. Pressure is force per unit area, measured in pascals (N/m²).

questions.q: A block of metal has a mass of 600 g and a volume of 75 cm³. Calculate its density in g/cm³.
A copper sample has a density of 8900 kg/m³ and a volume of 0.002 m³. Calculate its mass.
questions.explain: Rearranging ρ = m/V gives m = ρV = 8900 × 0.002 = 17.8 kg.

questions.q: Water has a density of 1000 kg/m³. What is the mass of 0.5 m³ of water?
An object of mass 240 kg has a density of 600 kg/m³. Calculate its volume.
questions.explain: Rearranging ρ = m/V gives V = m/ρ = 240 ÷ 600 = 0.4 m³.

questions.q: A solid object floats on water. What can you conclude about its density?
options: It is greater than the density of water
It is equal to the density of water
It is less than the density of water
It has no density because it floats
questions.explain: An object floats when its mean density is less than that of the fluid (water, 1000 kg/m³); denser objects sink.

questions.q: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 5.0 m in water (density 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 N/kg).
questions.explain: p = hρg = 5.0 × 1000 × 9.8 = 49 000 Pa. Pressure in a fluid increases with depth, density and gravitational field strength.

questions.q: As you go deeper into a liquid, what happens to the pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure in a fluid increases with depth because there is a greater weight of fluid above pushing down (p = hρg).

questions.q: What causes atmospheric pressure at the Earth's surface?
options: The weight of the air above pressing down
The magnetic field of the Earth
questions.explain: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of the column of air above a surface. It decreases with altitude because there is less air above you.

questions.q: What happens to atmospheric pressure as you climb to a higher altitude?
questions.explain: As altitude increases there is less air above you, so the weight pressing down is smaller and atmospheric pressure decreases.

questions.q: An object floats when the upthrust acting on it is:
questions.explain: When floating, the upthrust (upward force from the fluid) balances the object's weight, so the resultant force is zero. If weight exceeds the maximum upthrust, the object sinks.

questions.q: What is the cause of the upthrust that a fluid exerts on a submerged object?
options: Pressure is the same everywhere on the object
Pressure is greater on the bottom of the object than on the top
The object's weight pushes the fluid up
questions.explain: Pressure in a fluid increases with depth, so the upward pressure on the bottom of the object is greater than the downward pressure on the top. This pressure difference gives a net upward force called upthrust.

questions.q: In the required practical, a regular block measures 2.0 cm × 3.0 cm × 5.0 cm and has a mass of 240 g. Calculate its density in g/cm³.
questions.explain: Volume = 2.0 × 3.0 × 5.0 = 30 cm³. Density ρ = m/V = 240 ÷ 30 = 8 g/cm³.

questions.q: In the density required practical, how is the volume of a small irregular stone best measured?
options: By measuring its length with a ruler
By using a displacement (eureka) can or measuring cylinder to find the volume of water it displaces
By weighing it on a balance
questions.explain: An irregular solid has no simple shape, so its volume is found from the volume of water it displaces when fully submerged (using a measuring cylinder or displacement can).

questions.q: A stone is lowered into a measuring cylinder. The water level rises from 50 cm³ to 75 cm³. The stone's mass is 60 g. Calculate its density in g/cm³.
questions.explain: Displaced volume = 75 − 50 = 25 cm³. Density ρ = m/V = 60 ÷ 25 = 2.4 g/cm³.

questions.q: Two objects have the same mass but object A has a larger volume than object B. Which statement is correct?
questions.explain: For the same mass, the smaller volume gives the larger density (ρ = m/V). So object B, with the smaller volume, is denser.

questions.q: A force of 60 N acts on an area of 0.0030 m². Calculate the pressure produced.
questions.explain: p = F/A = 60 ÷ 0.0030 = 20 000 Pa. A small area concentrates the force, giving a high pressure.
